name: Foundational freelance-platform and front-company revenue model tied to the Munitions Industry Department

attribution.legal_posture: Defensive synthesis of cited public sources; the technique mapping supplies context rather than an identity attribution.

caveats: False-positive caution: Family accounts, payroll processors, employer-of-record services, and lawful remittance providers may create third-party routing. Obtain consent and follow financial/privacy law.

False-positive caution: New and small firms, international vendors, and freelancers can have sparse records; sparse records can occur in legitimate activity, and fraud requires evidence beyond footprint size.
The report’s counts and revenue estimates are Member State assessments from 2019; they require newer reporting before projection to 2026.
The ASIS “Follow the Money” reference has a source title without reviewed article text; revenue figures and organizational relationships require the underlying article.

statements: UN S/2020/151 reports at least 1,000 dispatched IT workers as of November 2019, use of subordinate entities/front companies, concealed accounts on freelance developer platforms, a rough $5,000 monthly worker average with about one third channelled to the DPRK, and operations targeting clients in multiple countries.
